newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechens arrive in Moscow for economic talks.
newsitem.headline: Chechens arrive in Moscow for economic talks.

text.p: A government delegation from breakaway Chechnya, which fought a 21-month war with Moscow, arrived in the Russian capital on Sunday for talks on economic cooperation, Itar-Tass news agency said.

Chechen First Deputy Prime Minister Movladi Udugov told Tass his delegation, which includes oil, banking and customs officials, would meet Russian First Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais on Monday.
The Chechen delegation will also have talks with Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin and Anatoly Kruglov, head of the state customs committee, Tass said.
Udugov said the main aim of the talks was to resolve questions for completing agreements on banking, customs and transporting oil across the separatist southern region.

The talks are part of efforts to build a lasting peaceful relationship following the conflict over Chechnya's independence drive. Tens of thousands of people died in the fighting before a ceasefire was agreed last August.

Under a peace deal, Russia has withdrawn its forces from Chechnya and agreed to defer until 2001 a decision on whether the region should become independent -- the issue at the heart of their conflict.
Talks are now focused on economic issues, including control of a pipeline that runs across Chechnya and will deliver oil from Azerbaijan's new off-shore deposits to Black Sea ports.
Russia signed a memorandum with Chechnya on June 13 on transporting oil across the breakaway region, but no final deal has been signed yet.
